findings.finding: Inspected score PDF pages 1–2, 4, 6–8, 10, 12 and 14 across slow and fast sections. Three independent single-note lines exchange imitative semiquaver figures; the first violin has somewhat more upper-register melodic work, but the technical burden circulates. Slow chromatic suspensions demand careful ensemble intonation.

grade.basis: Upper-intermediate overall: modest violin range and largely scalar single-line passagework, without advanced double-stop or sustained high-position demands. The Allegros require clean semiquaver articulation and independent entries, while the slow sections expose chromatic tuning and bow control. Individual technique is around level 2; one level of ensemble uplift accounts for equal-voice contrapuntal coordination and exposed tuning.

findings.finding: Inspected all three music pages of cello I, covering the complete Serenade and Humoreske, plus sampled music pages of cellos II–IV. Cello I sustains the highest melodic writing, with tenor/treble-clef changes, upper-position and thumb fingerings, chromatic shifts, trills, slurred/staccato running figures and some double stops. Cello II shares substantial mobile upper writing; lower parts are generally less demanding.

grade.basis: Advanced cello technique across the pair: the Serenade requires poised upper-register cantabile, shifts and double-stop intonation, and the Vivace Humoreske adds sustained mobile passagework, mixed articulation and quick pizzicato/arco changes. This is around ABRSM 8/RCM 9 for the first cellist; the ensemble requires matched attacks, balance and responsive tempo changes, but does not warrant a further level above the hardest part. The two pieces use contrasting major tonalities (D and F).
